title: Ruffino's two sets of books and how many records Ridgley made
summary: Ruffino paid small sums, no royalty statements and kept two sets of books; records kept Ridgley's name alive, perhaps in the 50s counted.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: So was that, uh, did you ever see any money when you were with Joe Ruffino? Oh, what level?
I go there and sometimes I get maybe a hundred dollars or so like that. And that was nothing big. No money.
I mean, did he ever show you a royalty statement? You know, sales? No, no royalty, no.

No, no, no. No, no. What I learned about Joe Ruffino, Joe would show us a book with the loss and he had the other book. See, he had two set of books. I learned this too. Because his secretary said she used to tell him, Joe, you shouldn't do it like that. Because he had two set of books. What you gonna do?
So what you looked at is that those records kept you working.
They kept me working. You know what? They kept my name flourishing quite a bit. And you see, I'm looking at that. That's quite a few records.
Yeah, you've made a lot of records over.

Now, you know, I was talking to Oliver Morgan. Oliver Morgan said, how many? And see, this is not all. See, because we don't talk, we're gonna get together and talk about this other album, the one that just came out with Imperial. Oh, okay. We talked about that one. We did? Okay. Yeah, we talked about those songs. Okay. Yeah, we talked about all that. But you see, Oliver asked me, he said, man, how many records have you recorded? I said, I couldn't give you a figure. I said, really? I don't know. I said, I know I recorded quite a few. And so I tried to count them. I think about, it's in the 50s.
